A single machine glows from within, its cyan edge-light raking across the polished floor in a cold wash; above it, a rotating beacon sweeps magenta arcs across the ceiling ducts and the chrome kick-rail below.
A bank of machines off to the left throws a massed amber-gold wash across the wet mat inside the doors, every puddle on it holding a long smear of warm orange against the surrounding blue-black.
A row of nine round bulbs along a ceiling beam burns warm amber, each small globe repeated in the lacquered floor below; the gaps between them fall into deep teal shadow.
A rotating beacon on a machine top sweeps rose-red light slowly round the room, catching the underside of a ceiling duct in each pass and leaving the chrome levers it crosses briefly gold.
A lit prize shelf glows from underneath, rimming every soft toy's fur in warm gold while the wall behind them sinks into a saturated violet-blue.
A vending machine at the far end of a blue-black run throws a warm amber square onto the floor in front of it, its sides raking back into cool indigo shadow.
A bare fluorescent tube over the change counter casts a cold blue-white pool across the counter's chrome lip while everything beyond it holds deep magenta.
A mirrored pillar near the centre doubles every coloured glow in the room, its surface alive with layered cyan and orange reflections that have no single source.
The wet floor inside the open doors carries the street's night colours upward in long smeared streaks of cool blue-violet against the warm amber that radiates from deeper inside the room.
A clear dome full of capsules sits lit from below; inside it, yellow, red and green capsules stack up, their colours tinting the chin and cheekbones of a face bent over them from above.
A run of little coloured lamps along a machine's edge blinks unevenly — five of the nine are lit in alternating cyan and rose, the dead ones leaving small cold gaps in the line.
One machine stands dark and unplugged in the middle of the row, a black void absorbing the cyan wash that spills around its flanks from the glowing machines on either side.
A low amber worklight in a back corner where a machine is pulled out throws a warm ochre pool across the dusty floor behind the gap, the pulled-out machine's chrome back raking through it.
A cluster of eleven coloured bulbs strung along the ceiling grid sways very slightly, dragging their spots of red, green and deep blue across the ceiling ducts in slow ovals.
A curtained booth leaks warm rose-gold light round the edges of its heavy curtain, the surrounding floor taking that colour while the ceiling above it stays a flat blue-black.
A stair head opens in the floor, cooler blue-green light spilling up through it and washing the underside of the landing above in a teal that cuts against the amber of the room around it.
A single hanging shade low over a bench throws a tight warm-gold pool onto the bench surface and the forearms resting there, leaving the surrounding floor in deep blue-violet.
A wall of glass tops all lit from inside sends light upward through them in a pale aquamarine sheet that tints the chrome claw cables hanging above each one in cold blue.
The doorway to the street at the far end fills with cool blue-violet night colour that spills across the floor in a wide cold patch, everything nearer burning amber and rose by contrast.
Coin-slot lamps low along a whole row of machines run at knee height, a line of small warm-orange glows cutting along the polished floor and leaving the space above them in deep indigo.
A clear plastic capsule column glows from an internal lamp; the stacked capsules above the glow burn red, green and yellow in turn, and a face bent close is lit from below in shifting warm colour.
A massed glow from an unseen bank of machines off to one side washes the floor in a broad sweep of teal, and the chrome levers of the nearest machine reflect it back in cold blue-green.
Seven round bulbs along a beam glow warm gold against a ceiling painted deep blue by the cool fluorescent wash from the other end of the room, the two colours meeting at the duct between them.
A rotating beacon sweeps cyan light across a mirrored pillar every few seconds, and the pillar throws it back doubled and slightly widened, so the far wall pulses between cyan and near-black.
A lit prize shelf beneath a row of soft toys rims each toy's fur in warm rose-gold from below while the wall behind them holds a deep blue-green from a machine's massed glow off to the side.

A strip of rose-pink neon tubing mounted along the baseboard runs the full length of one wall, its glow pooling in a low warm band across the polished floor while the machines above it hold in deep indigo shadow.

Backlit buttons on a control panel burn in a tight cluster of red, amber and green, each one casting a small coloured halo onto the machine's dark fascia and reflecting a dim twin in the chrome coin tray below.
Fluorescent tubes inside a drop ceiling grid throw a flat cold blue-white across the centre of the room while the far corners hold dense amber from the machine banks piled there.
Two machines face each other across a narrow aisle, each throwing its cyan edge-light toward the other so the gap between them fills with a layered blue-green brighter than either machine alone.
An emergency exit lamp in the far corner burns a steady deep red, its cone reaching low across a stretch of empty floor and tinting the chrome base rail of the nearest machine in dark rose.

A glass ticket-counter display runs along one side, lit from a cold internal tube; its top surface sends a thin aquamarine sheet upward that washes the ceiling tiles directly above in pale blue-green.

Overhead track lights aimed at a prize wall cast tight warm-gold cones onto the shelves, each cone hard-edged against the surrounding blue-black ceiling and leaving clean shadows behind every displayed object.

A hanging cable of small carnival bulbs looping between two posts blinks on in sequence, rolling a wave of warm amber dots along its length and scattering tiny golden pools across the floor beneath the loop.
A machine's attract-mode screen floods its immediate surroundings in shifting blue and violet, the pulses moving across the floor in slow rhythmic sweeps every few seconds as the animation cycles.
The underside of a mezzanine above the rear of the room is lit by uplights below, its surface burning in a warm copper-gold that cuts sharply against the cool blue-green ceiling beyond its edge.
A power strip on the floor behind a machine leaks a thin line of red pilot-light glow along the baseboard, the only warm colour in a stretch of floor otherwise held in deep teal from above.
Chrome edges along a row of machine tops catch the overhead fluorescent wash and send it back as a chain of cold blue-white highlights running the length of the row at eye height.

A large aquarium built into one wall is lit from within by cool blue tubes; the glow spreads outward in a broad teal rectangle across the surrounding wall surface and the floor immediately in front of it.

Spotlights recessed into the floor at the base of a mirrored wall shoot cold white beams upward, each beam widening as it climbs and meeting the ceiling as a broad pale oval against the surrounding indigo.

The ceiling above the main entrance is ringed with small coloured downlights in a circle, each throwing a separate red, green or blue pool onto the floor below and the rings overlapping in complex mixed colours at their edges.
A neon ring mounted flat on the ceiling above a central machine cluster glows a steady rose-red, its colour washing downward in a wide soft cone that deepens to magenta at the machines' chrome tops.

A single bare bulb on a long pendant drops low over a corner machine, its warm amber spilling sharply onto the machine's top glass and pooling on the floor beside it while the ceiling above stays entirely black.

A blacklight tube mounted inside a ceiling recess sends invisible ultraviolet downward and the polished floor beneath it blooms in a cold blue-white that makes every scuff mark glow against the dark surrounding surface.

Coloured gels taped over a pair of wall-mount fluorescents split the rear wall down its centre, one half burning in deep amber and the other in cool teal, the two colours bleeding into each other along a soft vertical seam.

A ring of blue LEDs around the base of a large claw machine sends a flat cold wash across the floor in a near-perfect circle, the chrome feet of adjacent machines catching its edge in bright blue-white points.
Prize tokens stacked in a lit dispenser column glow amber through their translucent housing, the column acting as a narrow vertical lamp that casts a warm stripe up the wall immediately behind it.

A drop of condensation on a cold machine side catches the surrounding cyan glow and holds it as a single bright bead, its reflection on the polished floor directly below a precise dot of the same cold blue-green.

Pendant lamps over a row of seating benches along the side wall alternate warm gold and cool white, the two colour temperatures banding the wall behind the benches in stripes of amber and blue that meet at each lamp's midpoint.

A wide vent grille near the ceiling carries a faint warm amber glow through its slats from the mechanical room beyond, each slat throwing a thin horizontal bar of warm light across the duct face opposite it.

A floor-level service indicator lamp on a machine's side panel pulses slowly between off and a deep amber-orange, each pulse sending a brief warm wash across the neighbouring machine's chrome base rail before fading back to dark.

An exit sign box mounted high on the back wall bleeds a steady red-orange glow downward onto the top edge of the machine beneath it, the chrome casing catching it as a thin hot stripe while the floor below holds cool teal.

Four strip lights tucked beneath a suspended ceiling panel throw their cold blue-white wash sideways across the duct work, leaving a sharp shadow line where the panel ends and the amber from the floor machines begins.

A string of small teardrop bulbs looped between two ceiling columns burns a warm rose-gold, each bulb's twin hanging motionless in the lacquered floor below, the space between the columns held in deep indigo.
The underside of a low mezzanine edge catches the cyan from the machines below it and holds the colour along its full length, a cold blue bar floating above the warm amber of the main floor.
One prize capsule column in the corner pulses its internal lamp in a slow rhythm, the brief bright intervals washing the near wall in alternating yellow-white and deep violet as it dims back down.

A chrome ceiling grid above the central aisle reflects a dozen different coloured glows simultaneously, its bars each carrying a different colour — rose, amber, teal — as though lit from twelve directions at once.
The knee-level gap beneath a long row of machines glows faintly amber from the power-indicator strips inside, a continuous warm band running the length of the row just above the polished floor.
A glass trophy case against the side wall is lit from a recessed lamp inside its top edge, the cool white light descending through the case and casting a pale rectangle onto the floor in front of it.

Condensation on the inner face of the front window catches the room's layered colours and holds them in a soft smear — warm amber low, shifting rose mid-height, cold blue-violet at the top where the ceiling wash reaches.
A ceiling-mounted rotating mirror ball turns slowly at the far end of the room, scattering small oval patches of cyan, amber and rose across the machines and floor below in a slow continuous drift.

Two machines set back-to-back share no gap between them, and the glow from each one rakes along their joined side in opposite colours — cold teal from the left, warm amber from the right — meeting at the seam.

The chrome pole of a stanchion rope picks up a long vertical stripe of magenta from the beacon behind it and a shorter stripe of cold blue-green from the machine ahead, the two colours dividing it cleanly in half.

A shallow step between two floor levels catches warm amber light on its top surface and holds deep teal in the riser below it, the edge between the two colours sharp and horizontal across the whole width of the room.
Dust motes above the central aisle drift through a diagonal shaft of warm amber light from a machine's top lamp, each one briefly gold before passing back into the surrounding cool blue-black.

A cluster of three machines in the corner forms a triangle of overlapping glows — amber, rose and cyan — each pair of colours combining in the overlap zones to make a shifting secondary wash on the ceiling above them.
The chrome flip-lid of a coin return slot catches the room's massed amber glow and holds it as a small concentrated oval of warm gold against the darker body of the machine around it.

A service hatch left open in the back wall lets a thin cold blue-white strip of utility light cross the floor from its edge to the nearest machine's flank, cutting through the ambient amber at a low angle.
An internal lamp in a low round machine burns through its translucent top dome, washing the dome's rim in warm gold and sending a diffuse upward cone of yellow-white toward the ceiling duct above it.

The chrome underside of a canopy overhang above a machine row takes the amber from below and the cool fluorescent from above simultaneously, its surface carrying both colours in parallel bands that shift as the beacons move.

One whole side wall is painted deep blue by the massed cool glow of the machines along it, and the ambient amber from the centre of the room catches only the wall's textured surface imperfections, picking them out in tiny warm dots.

A power strip running along the baseboard behind a pulled-out machine glows its indicator lights at floor level — a row of tiny red and green points barely above the ground, their colour lost in the larger amber above.
The ceiling directly above the open stair head is washed in the cooler blue-green rising from below, a distinct cold oval floating against the amber ceiling panels on every side of it.

Three machines along the back wall have their top lamps aimed inward rather than up, and the resulting crossed beams of amber and rose meet at chest height above the aisle floor in a warm overlapping patch.

A length of chrome kick-rail along the machine fronts picks up the beacon's rose sweep on one pass and the ambient teal from across the room on the next, alternating between the two colours in a slow steady rhythm.

The deep recess of a claw-machine interior glows from a cold white lamp at its top, the light falling through the tangle of soft toys inside and casting their shadows downward onto the glass floor of the cabinet in layered warm shapes.

Neon flex tubing stapled along the skirting board runs the full length of the far wall in a continuous ribbon of deep magenta, its reflection sliding unbroken across the lacquered floor beside it like a second strip of colour.

Emergency lighting strips recessed into the ceiling grid cast a cold green-white rake across the tops of every machine in the row, leaving their lower panels in the amber warmth that rises from the coin-slot lamps below.

Two UV tubes mounted above the prize counter flood a narrow band of the room in violet, turning the pale trim strips on the nearest machines a vivid white-blue against the warm amber beyond their reach.

A hanging lantern of red-tinted acrylic sways on a long cable above the central aisle, throwing a rose oval that drifts slowly across the polished floor and climbs the flank of each machine it passes.
The ceiling above a bank of fighting machines burns deep orange from the screen-glow rising off them, while the duct work crossing that orange ceiling pulls a sharp black silhouette against it.
A column of stacked disc-shooters glows along its full left edge in cold cyan, and the chrome coin tray at its base collects that colour into a small bright pool against the surrounding floor shadow.
Strip lights inside a low display counter turn the glass top into a luminous pale-gold slab, and every chrome hinge along its edge catches that warmth while the floor around it stays deep indigo.

Ropes of small orange-amber bulbs drape between two ceiling pillars in a shallow catenary, their combined glow warming the air between the pillars and leaving both outer aisles in comparative blue-black cool.

A large floor fan near the wall catches the cyan machine-glow on its rotating grille, splitting it into brief strobing arcs that move across the floor tiles in a fast shallow sweep with each blade pass.

The underside of a mezzanine balcony above the row is washed entirely in rose from the machines below, and the steel bolts along its soffit each carry a tiny hot-pink highlight against the surrounding blush.

Spotlights recessed into a low dropped-ceiling section above the change booth pour cold blue-white cones straight down, cutting crisp round pools on the counter below while the booth's side walls hold warm amber.
A wall-mounted trophy cabinet glows from a single internal strip at its top, lighting the row of chrome cups inside from above and sending a thin wedge of warm gold out through the gap at its base.

Four machines in a close cluster share a massed screen-glow that bleeds upward in shifting blue-green, and where their light meets the amber beacon above it forms a narrow lime band across the ceiling duct between them.

A broken overhead lamp leaves a gap in the ceiling grid where darkness pools, and the machines on either side send their cyan and amber upward into that gap, meeting in a dim neutral wash at its centre.

A back wall covered in brushed aluminium panels returns the room's mixed colour in a broad diffuse sheet, warmer orange near the floor and cooler blue-violet higher up where the fluorescent counter-light reaches.
Coin-return buttons along a whole row glow in a steady warm amber, a low dotted line of small paired glows running at waist height and fading into the deeper blue-black between each machine cabinet.

A single red indicator lamp on top of a corner machine pulses slowly, and with each pulse it throws a brief red cast across the ceiling corner above it and the dust collected on the duct flange there.

The chrome handrail along the step down to the lower section catches every colour in the room sequentially as a rotating beacon sweeps past — cyan, then amber, then a moment of near-white before cycling back.

A string of paper-cased lanterns hung along the rear wall glows warm rose from inside each shade, their light falling in overlapping warm ovals across the dark wall between them and pooling on the shelf below.

Track lighting on a short run above the redemption counter aims three tight spots downward in cold white, and the shadow each lamp casts from the counter edge falls hard and blue-tinged onto the mat below.

Light from a machine's attract sequence pulses in a rapid alternation of cyan and deep magenta, and each pulse briefly paints the adjacent machine's black side panel in one colour before switching it to the other.

A glow-tube ring mounted around a prize-capsule machine's circular top frame burns steady warm rose, and the ring's reflection in the dome below it makes a second rose circle inside the capsule glass.

The air above a tight cluster of screens holds a visible haze of mixed colour — amber from the coin lamps below, cyan from the edge lights beside them — that softens the hard ceiling fixtures caught in it.
A short neon arc fixed to the wall between two machine rows burns cold blue-white and throws a fan of light across the floor that bleaches the nearest machine's black base panel to a pale grey-blue.

Footlights recessed flush into the floor along the main aisle cast upward-facing warm amber beams that rim the bases of every machine above them in gold and throw each cabinet's undercut into sharp deep shadow.
